hero.headline: Woman, 24, dies after Port St. Lucie scooter hit-and-run; enhanced charges expected
hero.body:
A 24-year-old woman has died from injuries suffered in a hit-and-run crash while riding an electric scooter in Port St. Lucie, police said Wednesday. Following her death, police said they anticipate the State Attorney’s Office will pursue enhanced or additional charges based on the circumstances and the outcome of the investigation.

Investigators identified the alleged driver as 18-year-old Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer. He was arrested and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, a second-degree felony, police said. The expectation of enhanced or additional charges follows the woman’s death at approximately 9:23 p.m. Tuesday.

The crash happened around 5:10 a.m. Monday near the intersection of Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Police said a vehicle struck the woman as she rode an electric scooter. Investigators allege the driver left without stopping to help her or notify law enforcement.

The department’s Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified the vehicle as a gray Chevrolet Tahoe and located it at a Port St. Lucie home, according to police. Investigators said Sanchez-Chasmer had been playing “ding dong ditch” with friends shortly before the crash. According to police, the group was leaving a home where they had been participating in the prank when the vehicle struck the woman.

hero.headline: Indian River County public schools, district offices closed Thursday over flood risk
hero.body:
All School District of Indian River County public schools and district offices will be closed Thursday, Nov. 19, because saturated ground and expected heavy rain could make travel unsafe for students and employees, district officials announced Wednesday. The district cited potential flooding and concerns about travel to and from schools in its decision to cancel classes and close offices.

“With ground conditions already saturated, we cannot be confident that students and staff will be able to travel safely to and from school,” the district said. “Weather conditions may also affect staff members' ability to report to work.” The closure comes about two weeks after prolonged rainfall caused significant flooding in Indian River County.

A flood watch for Indian River County remains in effect through Friday evening as another round of rain moves through the Treasure Coast. The National Weather Service forecast calls for a 95% chance of precipitation Thursday, with about 1.74 inches of rain possible. The National Weather Service is also reporting a high surf advisory and rip current statement for the area.

Indian River County officials have warned residents that roads not officially listed as closed could still have standing water or other hazards. Drivers should obey barricades and never attempt to drive through floodwater. District officials said they will continue monitoring conditions and release additional information through official district communication channels.

cards.headline: Indian River County extends emergency through Nov. 23 as more rain threatens flooding
cards.teaser: Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems as officials warned that saturated ground could leave more neighborhoods vulnerable to flooding.
cards.body:
Indian River County has extended its local state of emergency through Nov. 23 as crews prepare drainage systems for more rain. Emergency management officials warned that saturated ground could lead to flooding in areas that did not flood during the last storm. Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems across the county as officials prepared for the possibility of more flooding.

Officials are closely monitoring flood-prone communities, including Heritage Plantation, Whispering Palms, and areas near Highland Drive. Ryan Lloyd, Deputy Director and Emergency Management Chief for the Indian River County Department of Emergency Services, urged residents countywide to prepare for possible flooding. “There could be areas that flood that we're not expecting per se or that necessarily flooded in the past,” Lloyd said.

Lloyd also asked residents to avoid driving through flooded neighborhoods to look at the damage. “We also ask our residents to please not do flood tours where they're going out just by standing and looking on at flooded neighborhoods, as they drive through those neighborhoods,” Lloyd said. “It can create waves that actually go into the houses, and it can make the flooding even worse for residents.”

Earlier this month, flooding left neighborhoods inundated, roads impassable and traffic disrupted. As of Tuesday, the county reported two properties destroyed and seven with major damage from the previous storm. Another 65 properties had minor damage, and 97 others were affected. The county's emergency information center is open for questions about the flood threat. Residents can call 772-226-4000 for assistance.

hero.headline: Boil-water notice continues for 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
A precautionary boil-water notice remains in effect for approximately 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie despite fully restored water service following a water main break near Glades Cut Off Road. City officials said the notice will remain in place until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink.

The advisory affects customers in Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano, as well as properties along Glades Cut Off Road. Residents should continue boiling water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

A contractor working on a non-city construction project struck the 36-inch water main. Crews completed repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the system. Water quality sampling is underway, city officials said. Because of the large number of customers affected, officials said the advisory could extend beyond the initial 48-hour timeframe.

For Marcus Rowe, a sudden drop in water pressure was the first sign of trouble. “I went to turn on the faucet, and the water pressure was low. I was like, 'what's going on'?” The Rowe family has been relying on bottled water and boiling water for daily needs while the advisory continues.

cards.headline: Rain worsens Milton damage at Port St. Lucie home, homeowner says
cards.teaser: Caryn McGregor says water is entering through her ceiling, windows and vents as she awaits state repair assistance. A repair assessment documents unrepaired Hurricane Milton damage.
cards.body:
Recent heavy rain is worsening unrepaired Hurricane Milton damage at Caryn McGregor’s Port St. Lucie home, she said, as she waits for state assistance to repair or replace it. Water continues entering through the ceiling, windows and vents more than two years after the storm.

McGregor said her roof was damaged when Milton struck Florida in October 2024. She initially contacted her insurance company but could not afford the deductible, she said, and later sought help through the state’s Rebuild Florida Housing Repair and Replacement Program.

A repair assessment lists Oct. 9, 2024, as the date of loss and Jan. 6, 2026, as the home’s inspection date. It documents unrepaired storm damage and notes that McGregor reported plumbing problems since the hurricane. The proposed work includes repairs involving ceilings, walls, plumbing, siding, appliances, drywall and doors.

McGregor has been using buckets and towels to manage the water entering her home. She said water has damaged her washer, dryer and dishwasher, and she worries that parts of the ceiling could collapse. “I can't even have my son living here because the ceiling, I'm scared of it falling on him and hurting him,” McGregor said. She also expressed concerns about water and mold.

McGregor said repairs remain unfinished and that she has been told the project is waiting on permits before work can move forward. “They were supposed to help,” she said. “However they were going to rebuild or replace it, they were supposed to do that.”

Recent rainfall has added to her concerns about the damage. “I want them to help us fix our house,” McGregor said. “They said they were going to.”

hero.headline: Indian River County public schools, district offices closed Thursday over flood concerns
hero.body:
All School District of Indian River County public schools and district offices will close Thursday, Nov. 19, as expected heavy rain raises concerns about flooding and safe travel. District officials announced the decision Wednesday, citing ground that is already saturated and the potential for more rain to make trips to and from school unsafe. The closure applies to both schools and district offices. Officials said the decision centered on protecting students, families and employees as another round of wet weather approaches an area that experienced significant flooding about two weeks earlier.

Indian River County is under a flood watch through Friday evening as more rain moves across the Treasure Coast. The National Weather Service forecast puts Thursday’s chance of precipitation at 95%, with about 1.74 inches of rain possible. The district said the storm system was expected to affect Indian River, Brevard and Volusia counties early Thursday. The forecast follows prolonged rainfall that caused substantial flooding in Indian River County roughly two weeks ago. With the ground still saturated, district officials cited both the incoming rain and existing conditions in explaining why schools and offices would not open Thursday.

District officials said they could not be sure students and staff would be able to travel safely between home and school. They also warned that the weather could prevent employees from getting to work. The district identified the safety of students, their families and employees as its top priority in making the closure decision. Travel concerns extend beyond roads that have been formally shut down: Indian River County officials have cautioned that streets not included on official closure lists may still have standing water or other hazards. Drivers should respect road barricades and avoid trying to drive through floodwater, county officials warned.

Along with the flood watch, the National Weather Service is reporting a high surf advisory and a rip current statement for the area. Those coastal alerts accompany the forecast for additional rainfall, while the district’s stated reason for closing schools and offices is the concern about flooding and travel on already saturated ground. District officials said they would keep monitoring conditions and share further information through official district communication channels. The announced shutdown covers Thursday, Nov. 19, while the county’s flood watch extends through Friday evening. Families and employees should use the district’s official channels for any additional updates as officials continue assessing the weather.

cards.headline: Indian River County extends emergency through Nov. 23 as more flooding threatens
cards.teaser: Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems as officials warned that saturated ground could leave previously unaffected areas vulnerable to flooding.
cards.body:
Indian River County has extended its local state of emergency through Monday, Nov. 23, as officials prepare for more rain and the possibility of flooding in areas spared during the last storm. Emergency management officials said the ground is saturated and additional heavy rain could cause flooding beyond the neighborhoods already affected by recent storms.

Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems across the county. Officials are closely monitoring flood-prone communities, including Heritage Plantation, Whispering Palms, and areas near Highland Drive. Earlier this month, flooding left neighborhoods inundated, roads impassable and traffic disrupted.

Ryan Lloyd, Deputy Director and Emergency Management Chief for the Indian River County Department of Emergency Services, urged residents countywide to prepare for a possible flood event over the next 72 hours. He warned that flooding could reach unexpected locations, including places that had not flooded in the past.

Lloyd also asked residents to avoid driving through flooded neighborhoods to look at the damage. “It can create waves that actually go into the houses, and it can make the flooding even worse for residents.”

As of Tuesday, the county reported two properties destroyed and seven with major damage from the previous storm. Another 65 had minor damage, and 97 others were affected. The county's emergency information center is open for questions about the flood threat. Residents can call 772-226-4000 for assistance.

hero.body:

Police identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened Monday morning near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators said the woman was riding west on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard. Police said Sanchez-Chasmer fled without stopping to render aid to the woman. The Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified him and located the vehicle during its investigation.

Investigators also learned that Sanchez-Chasmer had been playing “ding dong ditch” just before the crash, police said.

hero.headline: Boil water notice continues for 21,000 western Port St. Lucie customers despite repairs
hero.body:
A precautionary boil water notice remains in effect for approximately 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie despite fully restored water service. City officials said testing requirements could keep the advisory in place beyond the initial 48-hour timeframe.

Water quality sampling is underway, and the notice will remain in effect until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink. Officials said the large number of customers affected could extend the advisory.

The notice followed damage to a 36-inch water main near Glades Cut Off Road. A contractor working on a non-city construction project struck the main. Crews completed repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the system.

The advisory affects customers in Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano, along with properties along Glades Cut Off Road.

Residents are advised to continue boiling water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

cards.headline: Free sandbag sites open in Fort Pierce, St. Lucie County ahead of heavy rain
cards.teaser: Residents can fill their own sandbags at four locations as public works crews clear drainage systems. Standing water from the last storm is adding to concerns.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County are offering free self-service sandbag sites as residents prepare for heavy rainfall this week, with some still facing standing water from the previous storm. County public works crews are inspecting swales and drainage systems, clearing them to address potential flooding.

The City of Fort Pierce is offering sand at Martin Luther King Jr. Dreamland Park and Jaycee Park. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents should bring their own bags and shovels. Residents have been filling sandbags at Dreamland Park to protect their homes.

St. Lucie County has also established self-service sandbag distribution points at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds West Parking Lot and Lawnwood Stadium Parking Lot. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated sand for the county sites. Residents can find updates about precautions at www.readystlucie.org or contact the Public Works Department for more information.

Lisa Powell, whose ditches remain full from the last storm, described her concern: “The water is just still standing there, up to the yard.” Recent flooding left parts of the county submerged and residents in the Creekside development trapped inside. Some used kayaks to navigate flooded streets, while others waded through the water.

Fredrick Reeves, whose home previously flooded, is using sandbags and mulch to try to block water from entering his house before the upcoming rain. During the earlier flooding, he put down clothes to soak up the water, but it continued flowing into the house. Reeves described the situation as “overwhelming.” Another resident whose crawlspace took on a foot of water was filling sandbags to cover the opening.

hero.headline: Boil water notice remains in Tradition and western Port St. Lucie as service returns
hero.body:
A precautionary boil water notice remains in effect for Tradition and western Port St. Lucie despite full restoration of water service after Tuesday’s major water main break. Water quality testing began Wednesday, and residents should continue boiling water until the city confirms it is safe to use without boiling.

The notice covers the Tradition area, including Western Grove, Riverland, Wilson Grove and Southern Grove, west of Interstate 95 to Becker Road. It also covers communities along Glades Cut Off Road, including Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano.

The city initially recommended a 48-hour precautionary boil water notice Tuesday at noon. City officials said the number of customers affected requires collecting and testing a significant number of samples before the notice can be lifted. Restored service does not end the boil water notice.

The break happened near Glades Cut Off Road when a contractor working on a construction project unrelated to the city damaged a 36-inch water main, according to city officials. Crews completed repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the main shortly afterward.

The city is investigating the incident and expects to pursue appropriate action to recover costs from those responsible. Updates will be posted at CityofPSL.com.

hero.headline: 24-year-old scooter rider dies after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run
hero.body:
A 24-year-old woman died Tuesday night from injuries she suffered when a vehicle struck her electric scooter in a Port St. Lucie hit-and-run, police said Wednesday. An 18-year-old has been charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, and police expect prosecutors to pursue enhanced or additional charges following her death.

The crash happened around 5:10 a.m. Monday near the intersection of Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators allege the driver left without stopping to help the woman or notify law enforcement. She died at approximately 9:23 p.m. Tuesday, police said.

The department’s Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified the vehicle as a gray Chevrolet Tahoe and located it at a Port St. Lucie home. Investigators identified Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer, 18, as the alleged driver. Police said he had been playing “ding dong ditch” with friends shortly before the crash. According to the department, the group was leaving a home where they had been participating in the prank when the vehicle struck the woman.

Sanchez-Chasmer was arrested on the charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, a second-degree felony, police said. Following the woman’s death, police said they anticipate the State Attorney’s Office will pursue enhanced or additional charges as appropriate based on the circumstances and the outcome of the investigation.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County schools, district offices closed Wednesday over flooding concerns
hero.body:
All St. Lucie County public schools and district offices are closed Wednesday over concerns about heavy rain and localized flooding. The district also canceled all aftercare programs, after-school activities and athletic events scheduled for Wednesday. It plans to announce Wednesday evening whether schools will reopen Thursday.

Officials are monitoring rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes. Updates about school operations will be posted on the district’s website and social media channels.

Residents must bring their own bags and shovels, then fill the bags themselves. Sand is available while supplies last. On Tuesday, the two truckloads at Lawnwood Stadium were nearly gone.

Glen Ferlance, who lives in Port St. Lucie, said flooding two weeks ago kept him from reaching his children. He had to park at a plaza because he could not cross the flooded area to see them. On Wednesday, he said he was preparing for more rain and welcomed the school closure.

Elsewhere on the Treasure Coast, Martin County canceled after-school activities. Schools in Indian River County remained open as of Wednesday morning.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie scooter rider dies after hit-and-run; charges could be upgraded
cards.teaser: The 24-year-old woman was critically injured Monday near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Police expect prosecutors to pursue enhanced or additional charges against the driver.
cards.body:
A 24-year-old woman critically injured while riding an electric scooter in a hit-and-run crash Monday morning in Port St. Lucie has died, police said. The driver faces a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, and police now expect prosecutors to pursue enhanced or additional charges.

The crash happened around 5:10 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Officers said the driver struck the woman and fled without stopping to provide aid or contact law enforcement.

Police identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer, 18. Investigators said he had been participating in a game of “ding dong ditch” with friends shortly before the crash. According to police, he struck the scooter rider while leaving a residence where the group had been carrying out the prank, then left the scene.

Investigators with the department’s Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified the vehicle involved as a gray Chevrolet Tahoe and located it at a residence. Sanchez-Chasmer was arrested and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, a second-degree felony under Florida law.

Following the woman’s death, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said it expects the State Attorney’s Office to pursue enhanced or additional charges as the investigation continues. In a news release Wednesday morning, police extended condolences to the woman’s family and loved ones.

hero.headline: Florida animal cruelty hotline draws more than 30 calls, leads to Bay County dog rescue
hero.body:
Florida’s new statewide hotline for reporting suspected animal abuse has received more than 30 calls and led to the rescue of an abandoned and neglected dog in Bay County, according to Big Dog Ranch Rescue CEO and founder Lauree Simmons.

Simmons said the Florida Statewide Animal Cruelty Hotline went live Monday. Big Dog Ranch Rescue, located in Loxahatchee Groves, operates the state-funded hotline.

Treasure Coast residents and people throughout Florida can report suspected abuse anonymously by calling 844-4-SOSPET (844-476-7738). The hotline is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and accepts reports of cruelty, abandonment and dog fighting.

Reports are turned over to law enforcement, animal control or a government agency for possible investigation. Simmons urged people who see animals being neglected or starved to call and report it.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools to stay open Wednesday despite heavy-rain concerns
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County will keep schools open on a regular schedule Wednesday, Nov. 18, for students and employees despite concerns about heavy rainfall. Extended Day and extracurricular activities will also operate, and absences will not be excused solely because of the weather.

The district announced its decision Tuesday afternoon. “Families are encouraged to make the best decision for their circumstances,” a district spokesperson said. Weather-related absences will follow standard attendance procedures.

Elsewhere on the Treasure Coast, St. Lucie County Public Schools announced Tuesday that schools would close to students and employees Wednesday. All afterschool activities, after-care programs and athletic events scheduled for Wednesday were canceled. A district spokesperson cited National Weather Service forecasts indicating the potential for significant rainfall and localized flooding, along with already saturated conditions. District officials will monitor rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes throughout Wednesday. A decision about reopening Thursday will be announced Wednesday evening, with updates on the district’s website and social media platforms.

John Carroll High School in Fort Pierce also announced a Wednesday closure because of the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding throughout the region. All school-sponsored activities, including athletics, practices, extracurricular programs and other events, were canceled. The private school anticipates resuming normal operations Thursday, Nov. 19, pending weather and road conditions. Administrators will continue monitoring forecasts and communicating with local authorities. All after-school programs and Clubhouse locations operated by Boys Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County will also be closed Wednesday.

The Martin County School District will keep schools and Extended Day open Wednesday, but all other after-school activities, athletic practices and events are canceled. Martin County officials will monitor weather conditions. All Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County locations are scheduled to reopen Wednesday and resume normal operating hours.

hero.headline: Martin County approves $200,000 flood investigation as more rain threatens Jensen Beach
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners approved shifting $200,000 from the county’s stormwater budget Tuesday to investigate whether development and drainage changes contributed to flooding in Jensen Beach, where damaged neighborhoods face another heavy rain forecast. Up to 12 inches of rain is forecast over three days as families continue recovering from flooding two weeks ago. Commissioner Blake Capps called the investigation “a good starting point” and said the county may need to expand the study beyond the initial $200,000.

County figures show at least 36 homes sustained damage, with estimated residential losses of $3 million. Commissioners estimated another $14 million in beach damage and at least $1 million in roadway damage. Along Cheri Drive, dumpsters line driveways and damaged belongings sit outside homes. Lisa French, her husband, Jeremy, and their two young sons are among those displaced. French said 3 to 6 inches of water remained inside her home for more than a week, causing mold to grow 3 to 4 feet up the walls.

Commissioners also approved recovery assistance through the state’s State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) program, including grants of up to $25,000 for income-eligible homeowners and loans of up to $75,000 secured by property liens. The grants reimburse eligible repairs, requiring homeowners to pay first. “We don't have $25,000,” French said. The income caps are $86,040 for a one-person household, $98,400 for two people and $122,880 for four. Capps said commissioners would need to examine options for residents who narrowly exceed those limits.

The county currently has $1 million in SHIP funding available, and commissioners warned it could run out quickly. Human Services Director Michelle Miller said the state has assured the county it will receive disaster relief funds. Residents packed Tuesday’s commission meeting seeking financial help and answers about the flooding. French said her home’s walls had been torn down and the last of its tile removed. “We just need somebody to step up,” she said. “We need funding.”

County crews are working around the clock to lower retention pond levels, deploy additional pumps and drain flooded properties. Martin County is distributing sandbags at Halpatiokee Regional Park, with a limit of 25 per person, and coordinating with the National Weather Service and Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM). Fire Rescue is standing by with multiple high-water rescue trucks. Commissioners said a Federal Emergency Management Agency representative is expected to visit Nov. 30 to assess damage, a potential step toward federal disaster assistance.

cards.headline: Martin County schools, Extended Day open Wednesday; other activities canceled
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District will keep schools and Extended Day open Wednesday while canceling all other after-school activities, athletic practices and events amid heavy-rain concerns.
cards.body:
The Martin County School District will keep schools and Extended Day open to students Wednesday, Nov. 18, but has canceled all other after-school activities, athletic practices and events because of anticipated rainfall. Martin County officials will monitor weather conditions. All Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County locations also will reopen Wednesday and resume normal operating hours. The announcements come as schools and after-school programs across the Treasure Coast set different schedules in response to forecasts of heavy rainfall and concerns about flooding.

St. Lucie County Public Schools will be closed to students and employees Wednesday, a district spokesperson announced Tuesday, Nov. 17. All afterschool activities, after-care programs and athletic events scheduled for Wednesday are canceled. The spokesperson cited National Weather Service forecasts indicating the potential for significant rainfall and localized flooding, along with already saturated conditions. “While there remains some uncertainty regarding the exact timing, location, and amount of rainfall,” the spokesperson said, the district determined a cautious approach was best for students, families and employees. Officials will monitor rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes throughout Wednesday. A decision about reopening Thursday will be announced Wednesday evening, with updates posted on the district’s website and social media platforms.

John Carroll High School in Fort Pierce also will close Wednesday because of the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding throughout the region. The private school said the decision followed Tuesday’s early dismissal and a review of forecasts and local flooding conditions. All school-sponsored activities Wednesday, including athletics, practices, extracurricular programs and other events, are canceled. The school anticipates resuming normal operations Thursday, Nov. 19, pending weather and road conditions. Administrators will monitor forecasts and communicate with local authorities. All Boys Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County after-school programs and Clubhouse locations also will be closed Wednesday.

The School District of Indian River County will follow a regular schedule Wednesday for students and employees, including Extended Day and extracurricular activities. In its Tuesday afternoon announcement, the district said teams had found no standing water affecting safe routes to bus stops. Families were encouraged to make the best decision for their circumstances. The district said weather-related absences would follow standard attendance procedures and would not be excused solely because of weather.

cards.headline: Martin County residents press commissioners for emergency shelter before more rain
cards.teaser: Residents urged commissioners Tuesday to open a public shelter for unhoused people and families displaced by flooding. Commissioners are discussing local and federal funding options.
cards.body:
Martin County residents urged county commissioners Tuesday to open an emergency shelter before more rain arrives, asking them to act rather than wait for federal help. Speakers sought a public shelter for both unhoused residents and families who lost their homes in this month’s flooding.

During public comment, residents said water was already returning to their streets. Some said their homes had flooded earlier this month. Yamila Rollan Escalona, founder and executive director of Yaya Por Vida, a grassroots harm reduction organization, said she emailed her comments Tuesday morning as water rose again in her neighborhood. She then attended the meeting to speak. She said her organization has been asking commissioners for emergency shelter for most of the year.

Rollan Escalona said some unhoused residents were still staying in campsites surrounded by standing water. She pointed to a 2024 state law banning sleeping on public property and urged commissioners to provide shelter for people displaced by the flooding as well as those already unhoused. With drains and the ground saturated, she said the need was urgent. She also raised concerns about the longer-term effects of losing homes and belongings, saying mental health services on the Treasure Coast are already hard to access. She warned that stress and hopelessness could contribute to overdoses and a return to substance use.

Commissioners are discussing local and federal funding options. Florida has asked President Donald Trump for a major disaster declaration for the flooding. According to the Florida Policy Institute, a federal disaster declaration requires FEMA to cover 75 percent of the response and recovery costs incurred by state and local governments. Several speakers urged commissioners to open a shelter before federal approval, arguing that the county could act on its own.

Martin County Emergency Management Director Sally Waite previously told commissioners that flooding affected 77 homes. Residents with damaged homes can report damage and complete a needs survey on the county’s flood recovery page. The county is distributing sand and sandbags ahead of the rain at Halpatiokee Regional Park, 8303 SW Lost River Road, from noon to 6 p.m. Each household can receive up to 25 sandbags. Residents will be asked for their name and address. The county asks residents to check its map for the pickup location inside the park.

Neighboring counties didn’t wait. Churches didn’t wait, one speaker said. hero.headline: 18-year-old arrested in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver was arrested after police said he hit a woman riding an electric scooter to work in Port St. Lucie and drove away without stopping. Police identified him as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer and said he faces a felony charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. The 24-year-old woman was still unconscious and in critical condition Tuesday, Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said. “We're deeply concerned for her recovery, and our thoughts are with her loved ones,” he said. Published reports citing law enforcement records said Sanchez-Chasmer was being held on a $5,000 bond.

The collision occurred Monday morning near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators said the woman was heading west along the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard. She had entered a crosswalk when a gray Chevrolet Tahoe turning left onto Southwest Feather Terrace hit her, according to police. She was wearing a helmet. A witness stopped to assist her, called 911 and recorded the SUV's license plate information. Police said investigators used that information to identify the vehicle and Sanchez-Chasmer as the driver. Two friends were riding with him at the time of the crash, investigators said.

Investigators said Sanchez-Chasmer and his friends had been playing “ding-dong-ditch” shortly before the collision. Niemczyk said they went to a friend's home and fled when the friend's mother answered the door. The chief said investigators believe those inside the Tahoe knew a collision had happened. Neither Sanchez-Chasmer nor either passenger called 911, according to Niemczyk. He said leaving rather than stopping to help was central to the criminal investigation. “Had they remained on scene, provided aid, it would have been a very different criminal outcome,” Niemczyk said. “There probably wouldn't have been criminal charges at that point.” Police have not announced charges against the passengers.

The crash also raised safety concerns for another young scooter rider who travels in the area. John Rogalewski, 15, said he rides an electric scooter to school and is sometimes out early in the morning. “I'm looking at my surroundings almost the whole time,” he said. “I'm making sure every time I have to cross the street that there's not a car coming up, and that it is my sign to go, no matter how long I have to wait to cross.” Police said the investigation into the collision remains open, and toxicology results are pending.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County schools close Wednesday as superintendent pledges flood review
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Schools canceled Wednesday classes with heavy rain in the forecast, and Superintendent Dr. Jon Prince promised to review the district’s decisions during the Nov. 2 flooding. The review follows criticism over a video showing a boy wading through chest-high water after getting off a school bus in Port St. Lucie.

Prince said the district will monitor the weather Wednesday and decide late Wednesday afternoon whether to cancel Thursday classes. He said the district will continue that approach until officials are sure students can safely return. Prince said he hopes Wednesday’s closure is an overreaction but does not want to take chances. “The ground is so saturated, but if the conditions worsen tomorrow, we don't want a repeat of what happened November 2,” Prince said.

The video from Nov. 2 shows the boy stepping off a school bus on SW Coleman Avenue and walking through floodwaters that reach as high as his chest. Critics have pointed to the video in questioning the district’s actions. Prince apologized Tuesday night for the stress families experienced. “It was very stressful for our families, and I certainly apologize for the stress that they went through on that day,” he said.

Prince said the flooding was unexpected and that decisions were based on information available at the time. He said every decision made that day is being analyzed. “We are going to review all our procedures, our policies to make sure that if there's anything that we could have done differently, that moving forward we will,” he said.

cards.headline: Free sandbag stations open in St. Lucie County ahead of heavy rain
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce’s two park locations are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents must bring their own bags and shovels as crews check drainage systems and clear them.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents preparing for heavy rain this week can fill sandbags at free self-serve stations while public works crews check swales and drainage systems, clearing them to address potential flooding. The City of Fort Pierce is offering sand at Martin Luther King Jr. Dreamland Park and Jaycee Park. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk, and residents should bring their own bags and shovels.

The county also has self-service sandbag distribution points at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds West Parking Lot and Lawnwood Stadium Parking Lot. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated sand for the county locations.

Residents have been filling sandbags at Dreamland Park in Fort Pierce to protect their homes. Resident Lisa Powell said her ditches remained full after the last storm, with standing water reaching her yard. “My ditches are full from the last storm, they haven't gone down, so this could be very bad. The water is just still standing there, up to the yard.” Recent flooding left parts of the county submerged. Residents in the Creekside development were trapped inside, with some using kayaks to navigate flooded streets and others wading through the water.

Fredrick Reeves, whose home previously flooded, is using sandbags and mulch to block water from entering his house before the upcoming rain. During the earlier flooding, he tried to soak up the water with clothing as it entered his home. Reeves described the situation as “overwhelming.” Residents can find updates about precautions at St. Lucie County’s emergency management portal, www.readystlucie.org, or contact the Public Works Department for more information.

“We're deeply concerned for her recovery and our thoughts are with her loved ones,” Niemczyk said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County estimates $60 million shortfall as crews prepare for flooding threat
cards.teaser: The preliminary estimate reflects Amendment 3’s additional homestead exemption. County crews are deploying again after storm work two weeks ago generated unbudgeted overtime.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County is estimating a $60 million revenue shortfall next fiscal year under Amendment 3, which increases the homestead exemption, as crews deploy for another threat of rain and flooding. County spokesman Erick Gill said the preliminary estimate comes as county leaders consider their budgets and the costs of storm preparation and response.

Gill said the estimated shortfall would grow to about $120 million once the exemption increases further. “We're looking at the early estimates in this next upcoming fiscal year to be about a $60 million shortfall and then about $120 million once the exemption goes up.”

Crews are being deployed across the county as they were two weeks ago, Gill said. He estimated that 50 to 100 staff members, including public works crews, worked in the field during that storm, generating unbudgeted overtime. “I think everybody is well aware now that this storm drain system was not designed for the flooding we're getting nowadays,” Gill said.

This week, the county offered residents free sand to bag as another round of November rain and flooding threatened Florida's east coast. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated the sand. Gill said other services cost money, with the coming Amendment 3 tax cuts already on county leaders’ minds.

WATCH REPORT BELOW: Flooding and Budget Worries on Treasure Coast He said crews are being deployed across the county as they were two weeks ago. 'There were probably 50 to 100 staff members out there, including crews in public works, out in the field working during the storm. That's unbudgeted overtime,' Gill said. This week, the county offered free sand , donated by Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials, for residents to bag. Other services cost money, and Gill said budgeting is already on the minds of county leaders now that the Amendment 3 tax cuts are coming. What is uncertain is how the loss of revenue will affect things like storm preparation and response. 'We still don't know what the total impacts will be for, you know, with Amendment 3 with the additional homestead exemption,' Gill said. 'We're looking at the early estimates in this next upcoming fiscal year to be about a $60 million shortfall and then about $120 million once the exemption goes up.'

hero.headline: Teen arrested after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run critically injures scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver has been arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury after a hit-and-run critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an electric scooter in Port St. Lucie, police said. Investigators identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer.

The crash happened Monday morning near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Police said the woman was riding westbound on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard when she entered a crosswalk and was struck by a gray Chevrolet Tahoe. Sanchez-Chasmer was making a left turn onto Southwest Feather Terrace, investigators said.

Police said Sanchez-Chasmer fled without stopping to render aid. The Port St. Lucie Police Department's Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified him and located the vehicle through its investigation. Investigators also learned he had been playing “ding dong ditch” just before the crash.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools to keep normal Wednesday schedules after weather checks
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County will keep its regular schedules Wednesday after reviewing weather conditions across the county. In an update issued at 5 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 17, the district said all schools and district operations would proceed as usual the following day. The decision applies to the school day as well as Extended Day programs and extracurricular activities. Families were advised that the regular Wednesday schedule would remain in place following the district’s assessment. The announcement also addressed attendance, saying that the district’s standard rules would apply to absences related to the weather.

District teams checked conditions throughout Indian River County before the announcement. They reported no standing water that would interfere with safe travel routes to bus stops. That finding was part of the weather assessment accompanying the decision to maintain normal operations. The district’s notice paired the countywide checks with confirmation that schools would follow their usual Wednesday schedules. For families preparing for the morning, the district’s direction was to plan around the regular school schedule. The transportation-related finding concerned access to bus stops, with teams reporting no standing water affecting those safe travel routes during their checks.

The regular schedule also extends to activities outside classroom hours. Extended Day programs will operate as usual Wednesday, and extracurricular activities will go forward under the district’s announced plan. Those programs were specifically included in the Tuesday evening update, along with classes and district operations. The announcement therefore covers both the regular school day and the additional programs identified by the district. Families with children attending Extended Day or participating in extracurricular activities can plan for those programs to follow their normal Wednesday schedules, consistent with the district’s decision to keep schools and operations running as usual.

At the same time, the district encouraged families to make the decision they consider best for their own children. That guidance came with a reminder that weather-related absences remain subject to standard attendance rules. An absence will not be excused solely because it is connected to the weather, according to the district’s notice. Families weighing whether to send a child to school Wednesday should keep that distinction in mind: the district encouraged them to decide what is best for their children, while also saying its normal attendance rules would still govern any weather-related absence that day.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County crews clear drains as more rain threatens flood-hit areas
hero.body:
Public Works crews are clearing drainage blockages and lowering water levels where possible in St. Lucie County as another round of rain threatens areas still recovering from flooding earlier this month. Crews are also inspecting drainage systems and checking waterways. The National Weather Service has issued a flood watch from Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening, with 3 to 6 inches of rain forecast and higher amounts possible in some locations. The ground remains saturated, increasing the risk of flooding even if rainfall is lighter than during the early November storms.

St. Lucie County public schools and district offices will close Wednesday, Nov. 18, after the district dismissed students two hours early Tuesday over flooding concerns. All after-school activities, aftercare programs and athletic events scheduled for Wednesday are canceled. District officials will monitor rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes throughout Wednesday. A decision on school operations for Thursday, November 19, will be announced Wednesday evening. The district said the forecast supported Tuesday’s early dismissal to get students home before the heaviest rain. School scheduling decisions draw on forecasts and information from the National Weather Service and Emergency Operations Center.

Two weeks ago, floodwaters stranded cars, trapped families and forced some residents to wade through deep water. Near Oak Hammock K-8, 7-year-old Ella Ghodooshim walked through chest-deep water with her mother, Thassia Rodrigues. Rodrigues described how quickly the flooding overwhelmed the neighborhood as parents struggled to reach their children. “It was pretty scary and in a matter of minutes we had everything just flood,” she said. Rhett Linton, a parent who recalled kayaking through the flooded intersection during the previous storm, welcomed Tuesday’s early dismissal. “I'm super happy that they are stepping up and taking precautions,” Linton said.

Officials are urging residents to plan ahead, monitor forecasts and local alerts, and limit unnecessary travel. Drivers should never enter standing or moving water, which can stall a vehicle and cause costly engine damage. If drivers cannot tell how deep the water is, they should turn around and find another route. Residents can report flooding concerns to St. Lucie County at flooding@stlucieco.org.

cards.headline: Free self-service sandbag stations open in Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce’s two park locations are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents must bring their own bags and shovels. County stations also require residents to bring supplies and fill their own bags.
cards.body:
The City of Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County are offering free self-service sandbag stations as residents prepare for heavy rainfall this week. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags to help protect their homes from potential flooding.

Fort Pierce’s stations are at Martin Luther King Jr. Dreamland Park and Jaycee Park. Residents are advised to bring their own bags and shovels. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents have been filling sandbags at Dreamland Park in preparation for the rain.

The county’s self-service distribution points are at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds West Parking Lot and Lawnwood Stadium Parking Lot. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags at those locations. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated sand for the county stations.

Public works crews in St. Lucie County are checking swales and drainage systems ahead of more severe weather. They are also clearing them. Recent flooding left parts of the county submerged and residents in the Creekside development trapped inside. Some residents used kayaks to navigate flooded streets, while others waded through the water.

Resident Lisa Powell said water from the last storm remained in her ditches. “My ditches are full from the last storm, they haven't gone down, so this could be very bad. The water is just still standing there, up to the yard.”

Residents can visit St. Lucie County’s emergency management portal at www.readystlucie.org for updates about precautions to take. They can also contact the Public Works Department for more information.

cards.headline: Driver arrested in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured e-scooter rider
cards.teaser: Tristan Sanchez Chasmer, 18, faces a charge of fleeing the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. Police said he and two passengers had just played a prank at a home about a mile away.
cards.body:
Police arrested 18-year-old Tristan Sanchez Chasmer in connection with a Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an e-scooter to work early Monday morning. Chasmer faces one count of fleeing the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and is being held on a $5,000 bond.

The crash happened near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Body camera footage shows officers responding to the scene, where the woman was found unconscious in the road. A witness called 911 and helped her before she was airlifted to a hospital. She remains in critical condition.

Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the driver left the scene without stopping to render aid or contact law enforcement. Detectives identified the vehicle and traced it to Chasmer. According to Niemczyk, Chasmer and two passengers had just ding-dong ditched a home about a mile from the crash site.

“He was trying to get away from playing a prank,” Niemczyk said. The chief said the two passengers exited the truck shortly after the crash. “They're aware that they hit something. I'll say that,” he said.

“We're deeply concerned for her recovery and our thoughts are with her loved ones,” Niemczyk said.

hero.headline: 18-year-old arrested in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver has been arrested on a felony charge after Port St. Lucie Police Department investigators say he struck a woman riding an electric scooter to work Monday morning and left the scene. Police identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer, who faces a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. The 24-year-old woman remained unconscious and in critical condition Tuesday, Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said.

The crash happened near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators said the woman was traveling west on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard and had entered a crosswalk when a gray Chevrolet Tahoe turning left onto Southwest Feather Terrace struck her. Police said she was wearing a helmet. “We're deeply concerned for her recovery, and our thoughts are with her loved ones,” Niemczyk said.

A witness stopped to help the woman, called 911 and obtained the SUV's license plate information, police said. Investigators used that information to identify the vehicle and Sanchez-Chasmer. Niemczyk said investigators believe the people inside the SUV realized a collision had occurred. “They're aware that they hit something. I'll say that,” he said.

Investigators said Sanchez-Chasmer had two friends with him and had been playing a “ding-dong-ditch” prank shortly before the crash. Niemczyk said they had gone to a friend's house and fled when the friend's mother came to the door. The chief said leaving the crash scene was key to the criminal investigation. “Had they remained on scene, provided aid, it would have been a very different criminal outcome,” Niemczyk said. The investigation remains active, and toxicology results are pending, according to police.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County schools, district offices closed Wednesday as flooding threatens
hero.body:
All St. Lucie County public schools and district offices will be closed Wednesday, Nov. 18, because of the threat of significant rainfall and localized flooding, the district announced Tuesday. Wednesday’s after-school activities, aftercare programs and athletic events are also canceled. A decision on whether schools will reopen Thursday is expected Wednesday evening.

The closure follows Tuesday’s dismissal of students two hours early as worsening weather raised flooding concerns. District officials said National Weather Service forecasts indicate the potential for significant rainfall, though the timing and location of the heaviest rain remain uncertain. The ground is already saturated following historic flooding that forced schools to close for three consecutive days, Nov. 4, 5 and 6, and left roads underwater.

“Given the already saturated conditions in our community, the District believes taking a cautious approach is in the best interest of our students, families, and employees,” district officials said in a statement.

Throughout Wednesday, district officials will monitor rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes. Families are encouraged to check the district’s official website and social media channels for updates on Thursday’s reopening decision.

John Carroll High School also announced it will close Wednesday, Nov. 18, because of the threat of heavy rainfall and flooding across the region. The decision followed an early dismissal Tuesday and a review of forecasts and local flooding conditions. All Wednesday activities at the school, including athletics, practices, extracurricular programs and other events, are canceled.

John Carroll anticipates reopening Thursday, pending weather and road conditions. Administrators will continue monitoring forecasts and coordinating with local authorities before making further decisions. The school will share updates through its official communication channels.

cards.teaser: Residents must bring their own bags and supplies to fill sandbags at four locations. Public works crews are checking and clearing drainage systems as more rain approaches.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County are offering free self-service sandbag stations as residents prepare for heavy rainfall this week following recent flooding. The City of Fort Pierce has stations at Martin Luther King Jr. Dreamland Park and Jaycee Park. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk, and residents should bring their own bags and shovels.

The county has established self-service sandbag distribution points at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds West Parking Lot and Lawnwood Stadium Parking Lot. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated sand for the county locations. Public works crews in St. Lucie County are checking swales and drainage systems, clearing them to prepare for more severe weather and potential flooding.

Residents filling sandbags at Dreamland Park described concerns about water remaining from the previous storm. “My ditches are full from the last storm, they haven't gone down, so this could be very bad. The water is just still standing there, up to the yard,” resident Lisa Powell said. Recent flooding left parts of the county submerged and residents in the Creekside development trapped inside. Some used kayaks to navigate flooded streets, while others waded through the water.

Fredrick Reeves, whose home previously flooded, is using sandbags and mulch to block water from entering his house before the upcoming rain. He said he tried to soak up the water with clothes during the earlier flooding, but water entered the house. Reeves described the situation as “overwhelming.” Residents can find updates about precautions at St. Lucie County’s emergency management portal, www.readystlucie.org, or contact the Public Works Department for more information.

cards.headline: 18-year-old arrested in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured e-scooter rider
cards.teaser: Tristan Sanchez Chasmer, 18, is being held on a $5,000 bond. Police say he left the scene after a crash that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding her e-scooter to work.
cards.body:
An 18-year-old was arrested in connection with a Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that left a 24-year-old woman critically injured while riding her e-scooter to work early Monday. Tristan Sanchez Chasmer faces one count of fleeing the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and is being held on a $5,000 bond.

The crash happened near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Body camera footage shows officers responding to the scene, where the woman was unconscious in the road. A witness called 911 and helped her before she was airlifted to a hospital. She remains in critical condition.

Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the driver left the scene without stopping to render aid or contact law enforcement. Detectives identified the vehicle and traced it to Chasmer. According to Niemczyk, Chasmer and two passengers had just ding-dong ditched a home about a mile from the crash site. “He was trying to get away from playing a prank,” Niemczyk said.

Niemczyk said the two passengers got out of the truck shortly after the crash, but neither they nor the driver called 911. “They're aware that they hit something. I'll say that,” he said. The two passengers are not facing charges.

hero.headline: 18-year-old arrested after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run critically injures e-scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver has been arrested after police say he left a crash that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an e-scooter to work in Port St. Lucie. The woman was in a crosswalk on SW Feather Terrace when she was struck Monday morning, police said.

Police identified the driver as Tristan Ray Sanchez-Chasmer, 18. He is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. The crash happened Nov. 16 at about 5:10 a.m. near the intersection of SW Gatlin Blvd. and SW Feather Terrace. The woman was on her way to the Wendy's where she works. She was rushed to a hospital and remained in critical condition and in a coma, police said.

A good Samaritan recorded the vehicle's license plate number and stopped to help the woman, according to police. Investigators used that information to determine that a Chevy Tahoe struck her and to identify Sanchez-Chasmer as the driver. Police said he had been playing a game of ding, dong, ditch with friends before the crash.

Katie Santana, a Port St. Lucie resident who lives near the intersection, expressed concern about the driver's decision to leave. “I think for somebody to just leave another human being on the side of the road who was possibly injured, to not stop and check on them, it's truly heartbreaking that somebody would make that decision,” Santana said. Police said the State Attorney's Office would decide whether Sanchez-Chasmer could face a more serious charge if the woman dies.

We spoke with a high school student who rides an e-scooter in the area where the crash occurred. "I get a little bit fearful sometimes, 'cause I'll see some people going through red lights, not paying attention when they're turning and I've almost been hit a couple times," said John Rogalewski, age 15. hero.headline: Heavy rain may disrupt Indian River County waste pickups, close disposal sites
hero.body:
Heavy rain and gusty winds may delay Waste Management curbside collections in Indian River County, where ongoing flooding and the threat of more heavy rain have kept the Emergency Operations Center at Level 2, or partial activation. The landfill and all five Customer Convenience Centers may close early or remain closed if conditions become unsafe. The county urges residents to keep collection carts out of flooded streets.

Waste Management collects recycling in blue carts countywide. Its garbage, yard waste and bulk waste collection services cover unincorporated Indian River County, Fellsmere, Sebastian and Indian River Shores. Residents in other cities and towns should check with their local governments for service updates. The potential collection delays come as the east-central Florida coast faces a Slight Risk, or Level 2 out of 4, for excessive rainfall. Localized flooding is possible, especially along the coast, and some areas could receive 4 inches or more of rain.

For collection day, the county recommends putting carts out by 6 a.m., keeping lids closed, bagging garbage and avoiding overfilled carts. Cardboard should be flattened and placed inside recycling carts, while yard waste should remain inside yard waste carts. Residents should bring carts back in as soon as possible after collection. Those instructions accompany the county’s warning against placing carts in the street when it is flooded, as heavy rain and gusty winds threaten to disrupt solid waste services.

Emergency services, human services and infrastructure partners are coordinating response and recovery efforts while the Emergency Operations Center remains partially activated. The county urges residents to avoid flooded roads and floodwaters, watch for rising water in low-lying areas, and monitor weather conditions and official updates. Officials across the region also urge residents to keep roadways clear for emergency responders and find a safe alternate route when they encounter flooding. Residents with flood-related questions or information can call the Emergency Information Center at 772-226-4000 during operating hours.

Police arrested an 18-year-old driver accused of leaving a Port St. Lucie crash that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an electric scooter Monday morning. He was charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened near SW Gatlin Boulevard and SW Feather Terrace. Police said a vehicle struck the woman and the driver fled without stopping to render aid. The crash prompted police to urge drivers to use alternate routes and allow extra travel time.

Detectives with the Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified the driver and located the vehicle involved, according to police. Investigators also learned that the driver had allegedly been participating in a "ding dong ditch" prank shortly before the crash.

A police briefing began at 2 p.m. Tuesday. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk was expected to discuss the arrest, provide additional details about the investigation and share an update on the woman's condition.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County, Fort Pierce offer self-service sand ahead of potential flooding
cards.teaser: Residents must bring their own bags and shovels to fill sandbags. County sand is available at two Fort Pierce locations while supplies last, and city stations are open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County and the city of Fort Pierce are offering self-service sand for residents concerned about potential flooding. Residents must bring their own bags and shovels and be prepared to fill their own sandbags. County supplies are available while they last.

The county’s two distribution locations are the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds west parking lot, 5601 W. Midway Road, Fort Pierce, and the Lawnwood Stadium parking lot, 2000 Virginia Ave., Fort Pierce. County officials said Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated four truckloads of sand, with two truckloads delivered to each location. Residents should also bring any other supplies they need to fill their bags.

The City of Fort Pierce is offering free self-serve sandbag stations at Martin Luther King, Jr. 25th Street and at Jaycee Park, at S. Ocean Drive and Melaleuca Drive. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents using the city stations should bring their own bags and a shovel.

For additional information about city sand distribution, residents can contact the Fort Pierce Public Works Department at 772-467-3794. The county’s emergency management website also offers information about preparing for severe weather and flooding.

hero.headline: Martin County plans high-water rescue vehicle deployment as heavy rain threatens
hero.body:
Martin County is preparing for heavy rain and potential flooding starting Tuesday afternoon, and the sheriff’s office plans to station high-water rescue vehicles in areas most likely to flood. County officials anticipate rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches, with some locations potentially receiving 8 to 12 inches. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is coordinating with the county’s emergency operations center to track rainfall and determine which roads could become hard to navigate. Placing rescue vehicles near vulnerable areas would help deputies get to people who need help at home or become stranded in their vehicles, the agency said.

Deputies are warning drivers not to continue onto roads covered by water because the depth can be misleading and damage beneath the surface may not be visible. Anyone whose usual route floods should find a safe alternative or stay in a safe place until conditions allow travel. Residents should not bypass road barriers or venture into flooded areas to check water levels. Officials are also asking people to leave roads clear for emergency crews. Martin County Fire Rescue says households should be ready to leave if flooding endangers their homes or neighborhoods and should prepare emergency supplies for everyone in the household, including pets. The county’s Community Information Center will provide information about flooding.

Preparations are also underway elsewhere on the Treasure Coast. Indian River County’s emergency operations center remains partially activated at Level 2 as officials address existing flooding and the threat of additional rain. Emergency services, human services and infrastructure agencies are coordinating response and recovery work. Residents can call the county’s Emergency Information Center at 772-226-4000 during its operating hours with flood-related questions or information. Rain and strong winds could delay Waste Management collections, and residents should keep collection carts out of flooded streets. The county’s landfill and five Customer Convenience Centers could close early or stay closed if conditions become dangerous.

In St. Lucie County, the fire district has high-water vehicles and a rescue boat available for flooding emergencies. Free sand is available while supplies remain at the County Fairgrounds, 5601 W. Midway Road in Fort Pierce, in the west parking lot, and at Lawnwood Stadium, 2000 Virginia Ave. Residents must bring bags, a shovel and any other needed supplies. County public safety officials also advise securing tarps, outdoor furniture and other loose belongings. Northeast winds of 25 to 30 mph are forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday, with coastal gusts reaching 35 to 40 mph. Strong winds blowing onshore can also produce hazardous surf and rip currents.

cards.headline: Joe Namath's Lucky Shuck planned for Jensen Beach's Rio Marine Village
cards.teaser: The waterfront restaurant will join Rio Marine Village, which broke ground Thursday in Jensen Beach. The development’s first phase is scheduled for completion in late 2028.
cards.body:
Joe Namath is bringing a new location of The Lucky Shuck Oyster Bar & Taphouse to Rio Marine Village in Jensen Beach. The 30-acre waterfront development in Martin County broke ground Thursday after more than five years of planning, with its first phase scheduled for completion in late 2028.

The restaurant, owned by Namath and his business partner Charlie Modica, will be among several waterfront dining and entertainment destinations at Rio Marine Village. Plans also call for a second outdoor dining concept.

"The Lucky Shuck has always been about good food, good people and being on the water," Namath said. "Rio Marine Village gives us a home right on the river, and I can't wait to see boats pulling up and families sitting down together."

The mixed-use development will feature 342 apartments, a 131-slip marina and more than a half-mile of public riverwalk. Other planned amenities include the Osprey Club, a waterfront wedding and event venue, along with a public park, boardwalk and beach. Kayak and paddleboard rentals are also planned.

Martin County commissioners unanimously approved the project's first two phases following years of community discussions. Construction is expected to begin this month.

hero.headline: Teen arrested in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver has been arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a Port St. Lucie crash that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an electric scooter, police said. Investigators identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer.

The crash happened Monday morning near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. According to investigators, the woman was riding west on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard. As she entered the crosswalk, a gray Chevrolet Tahoe driven by Sanchez-Chasmer struck her while making a left turn onto Southwest Feather Terrace.

Police said Sanchez-Chasmer left the scene without stopping to render aid to the woman. He was arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified Sanchez-Chasmer and located the Tahoe during its investigation. Investigators also learned that Sanchez-Chasmer had been playing “ding dong ditch” just before the crash, police said.

Police said the driver fled the scene and failed to stop to render aid to the woman. Lucie Police Department's Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer and located the vehicle through its investigation. hero.headline: St. Lucie County schools releasing students two hours early ahead of flood watch
hero.body:
Schools in St. Lucie County are releasing students two hours early Tuesday ahead of a flood watch that runs from Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening. Forecasters expect 3 to 6 inches of rain, with higher amounts possible in some locations, as crews clear drainage systems in areas still recovering from early November flooding. The school district is asking families to monitor its official channels for updates as weather conditions change.

The National Weather Service issued the flood watch for St. Lucie County. The ground remains saturated, increasing the risk of flooding even if rainfall is lighter than during the early November storms. Public Works crews are inspecting drainage systems, clearing blockages and lowering water levels where possible. Crews are also checking waterways as the next round of rain approaches.

Two weeks ago, floodwaters stranded cars, trapped families and forced some residents to wade through deep water. One video showed 7-year-old Ella Ghodooshim walking through chest-deep water with her mother near Oak Hammock K-8.

Officials are urging residents to plan ahead, monitor forecasts and local alerts, and limit unnecessary travel. Drivers should never enter standing or moving water because floodwater can stall a vehicle and cause costly engine damage. Drivers who cannot tell how deep the water is should turn around and find another route. Residents can report flooding concerns to St. Lucie County at flooding@stlucieco.org.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie faces renewed flood threat with 4 to 6 inches of rain forecast
hero.body:
Another 4 to 6 inches of rain could fall over the next few days in Port St. Lucie, threatening renewed flooding in neighborhoods still recovering from record rainfall two weeks ago. St. Lucie Public Schools announced a two-hour early release Tuesday.

County crews have been inspecting canals and drainage systems, clearing them ahead of the expected rain. Officials warn that the ground remains saturated from recent storms, meaning far less rain than usual could cause flooding in neighborhoods, streets and other low-lying areas. The school district announced the early dismissal to avoid a repeat of the flooding problems that affected students taking buses home earlier this month.

The earlier flooding stranded cars, trapped some families in their homes and forced others to wade through deep water. “It was horrible,” said Port St. Lucie resident Crisostomo Santiago Perez. “Water was on top of the cars almost, covering hoods.” With more heavy rain forecast, Perez said he planned to get supplies before flooding returned.

Freshman Noah Julian was among those caught in the earlier flooding. He stepped off his school bus to find his neighborhood along Coleman Avenue flooded. A video recorded by neighbor Martina Elieson spread quickly on social media, showing him swimming through floodwaters to reach his driveway. His father, Romeo Julian, expressed concern about alligators, snakes and sharp objects in the water.

Residents are encouraged to monitor local forecasts and prepare for changing conditions as the rain moves into the area.

hero.headline: Martin County sheriff weighs e-bike seizures, parent charges after Jensen Beach crash
hero.body:
The Martin County sheriff is considering seizing illegal e-bikes and pursuing criminal charges against parents who knowingly allow their children to ride them. The sheriff outlined the potential crackdown Monday after a Jensen Beach crash left a 14-year-old Port St. Lucie boy with catastrophic injuries.

The boy was struck Sunday near U.S. 1 and Northwest Goldenrod Road and was airlifted to St. Mary's Medical Center, where he was in stable condition, the sheriff said at a news conference. He and a friend had traveled roughly five miles from home on separate e-bikes before attempting to cross U.S. 1. The friend made it across, but a northbound vehicle with a green light struck the 14-year-old. The impact threw him approximately 50 feet, and his e-bike landed about 100 feet away.

Investigators determined the boy was riding a 3,300-watt electric bike, more than four times the 750-watt limit cited by the sheriff. The sheriff described the motorbike-style vehicle as illegal for street use. The boy was wearing a helmet, which the sheriff credited with helping him survive the crash.

The proposed seizures and potential charges against parents would represent tougher consequences following educational workshops, warnings and previous enforcement efforts. The sheriff said those efforts have failed to curb dangerous riding. Martin County has recorded 41 e-bike crashes this year, involving riders ranging in age from 7 to 80, according to the sheriff.

The Florida Highway Patrol is leading the crash investigation, with assistance from the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The School District of Indian River County will put all schools on a Modified Day schedule Tuesday because of anticipated heavy rainfall, the district announced Monday, Nov. 16. All extracurricular activities will conclude by 2:30 p.m. Extended Day will be available Tuesday morning but closed Tuesday afternoon.

Weather-related absences will be excused if conditions prevent students from attending school. “We understand that weather conditions may affect families differently across our community. Please make the decision that is safest for your family. If weather conditions prevent your child from attending school, the absence will be excused,” the district said in its Monday statement.

The district said it will share additional updates by 1 p.m. the day before any further schedule changes.

The National Weather Service issued a flood watch Monday for Indian River, Martin, St. Lucie and Okeechobee counties, beginning Tuesday afternoon and continuing through Friday evening. Tuesday’s forecast calls for scattered showers and a few thunderstorms, with a chance of heavy rainfall. Widespread showers, storms and rainfall are forecast Wednesday, when flooding is possible.
